posts.title: VW launches its first LiDAR-equipped electric SUV in China
posts.summary:
FAW-Volkswagen has launched the ID. AURA T6 electric SUV in China, starting at 129,900 yuan ($19,240) and offering a CLTC range of up to 660 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: FAW-Volkswagen launched the ID. AURA T6 electric SUV in China with a starting price of 129,900 yuan, marking a 4.4% reduction from its pre-sales level.
The vehicle features the CEA electronic architecture developed in partnership with Xpeng and utilizes Horizon Robotics' Journey 6H chip for advanced driver-assistance capabilities.

This model represents Volkswagen's first all-electric SUV in China to integrate LiDAR, signaling a strategic shift toward deeper collaboration with local Chinese technology firms to maintain market competitiveness.

posts.title: Epicland X9 to launch on September 24 as first model from Dongfeng-Huawei brand
posts.summary:
The Epicland X9 SUV measures 5,301 mm in length and starts at 299,800 yuan ($44,400) in pre-sales.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The Epicland X9, the inaugural model from the Dongfeng-Huawei joint brand, is set to launch on September 24 following strong pre-order momentum of over 20,000 units within 24 hours.
The large 3-row SUV is positioned as a direct competitor to the Aito M9 and Li Auto's Li L9, featuring Huawei's Qiankun ADS 5 assisted-driving system and HarmonySpace 6 cockpit.
The launch highlights the rapid expansion of Huawei's automotive ecosystem, with the company simultaneously supporting multiple brand partnerships including the upcoming Aistaland GX7.

posts.title: Toyota plans China-made extended-range EVs in 2027 to broaden lineup, report says
posts.summary:
Toyota plans to begin EREV production in China in April 2027 and raise output to about 400,000 units in 2028, Nikkei Asia reported.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Toyota reportedly plans to enter the Chinese extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) market in April 2027, with production targets reaching 400,000 units by 2028.
The strategic pivot aims to leverage Toyota's existing hybrid expertise to bypass the intense price competition currently plaguing the pure battery electric vehicle (BEV) segment in China.
Despite the expansion, the EREV segment faces headwinds, with recent data showing a 15.85% year-on-year decline in retail sales for the first eight months of the year.
